sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Global Water Withdrawal vs. Consumption**: **Withdrawal** is the total water removed from a source, while **consumption** is the portion of withdrawn water permanently evaporated, transpired, incorporated into products, or consumed by humans/livestock.
• **Sectoral Dominance**: **Agriculture** is the largest global and national water consumer, accounting for roughly 70-80% of total freshwater withdrawal in India, followed by **Industrial** and **Domestic** sectors.
• **Blue vs. Green vs. Grey Water**: **Blue water** refers to surface and groundwater; **green water** is soil moisture derived from precipitation; **grey water** is wastewater generated from domestic/industrial activities requiring treatment.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: **Falkenmark Water Stress Indicator** classifies countries based on renewable freshwater availability per capita (below 1,700 m³/person = water stress; below 1,000 m³/person = water scarcity).

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **North-West India (Punjab, Haryana, Western UP)**: Over-extraction of groundwater driven by free electricity and paddy cultivation, leading to 'Dark Zones' or over-exploited assessment units.
• **Peninsular India (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu)**: Basin-level deficits, reliance on hard-rock aquifers, and frequent meteorological droughts managed via tank irrigation and watershed development.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Fragmented institutional frameworks, power-water subsidy nexus, low water pricing, and absence of statutory backing for the Model Groundwater Bill.
• **Policy Interventions**: Shift from flood irrigation to **Per Drop More Crop** (Micro-irrigation: Drip and Sprinkler), aquifer mapping by CGWB, and conjunctive use of surface and groundwater.

items.title: Mnemonic for Sectoral Water Consumption Order in India
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **AID** (Agriculture, Industry, Domestic)
• **Decoded Meaning**: Agriculture consumes the most, followed by Industry, and finally Domestic use.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly eliminates incorrect order-based MCQs in environmental and economic surveys.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: 80-10-10 rule of thumb for India's water consumption rough percentages: ~80% Agriculture, ~10% Industry, ~10% Domestic.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that the 'Domestic sector is the largest consumer of freshwater globally and in India'. This is INCORRECT. Agriculture is overwhelmingly the largest consumer in both contexts.

Mains Value Addition: Quote Mihir Shah Committee recommendations on replacing the Central Water Commission (CWC) and Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) with a unified National Water Commission (NWC) for integrated basin management.

keyTakeaways: Agriculture accounts for the vast majority (~80%) of India's water consumption, making agricultural water-use efficiency the core pivot of national water security.

Spatial disparities are acute: North-West India faces severe groundwater depletion due to intensive paddy cultivation, while Peninsular India relies heavily on rainfall and hard-rock aquifer management.
Policy shifts must transition away from free power subsidies toward micro-irrigation adoption, crop diversification, and integrated river basin management.
